source: Kirklees HWL Pathways Aug 26 v2.1 (draft 15 Sept 2026)
notes: Converted by hand from the scheme pathways document. Edit this file to update the finder; it is re-read automatically. 'open' is false for schemes that are not live yet. 'audience' says who the scheme is for: individual, employer or organisation. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

services.name: elevate
services.whoFor: Young adults aged 18-26 in Kirklees who are not in education, employment or training and have health concerns.
locations: Brian Jackson House, 2 New North Parade, Huddersfield, HD1 5JP (elevate connect, Wednesdays 1-3.30pm)
Jo Cox House, Batley (elevate connect, Tuesdays 1-3pm)
eligibility: Aged 18 to 26
Not in education, employment or training (NEET) with health concerns

activities.name: Community programme
activities.summary: Weekly group session plus weekly drop-in to build friendships, confidence, life skills and wellbeing. Activities co-designed with young people, such as yoga and gardening, arts and crafts, outings and volunteering.
activities.duration: Weekly group session, plus weekly drop-in

activities.name: Employability programme
activities.summary: One-week programmes for young people at risk of becoming NEET or unsure about career options. Mornings cover CV writing, interview preparation and job searching; afternoons have workshops and guest speakers. Breakfast, lunch and travel support provided. Key worker support and a 10 day work placement.
activities.duration: One-week programmes, running multiple times a year

services.name: Employment Kirklees
services.organisation: Paddock Community Trust, in partnership with Kirklees Council
services.whoFor: Anyone living in Kirklees, in or out of work, looking for employment support close to home.
locations: Paddock Trust bases in Huddersfield and Batley
Community settings across Kirklees - libraries, community and faith centres, schools and other accessible public venues
eligibility: Lives in Kirklees, whether employed or unemployed
Looking for support into work, apprenticeships, in-work progression or self-employment, or looking for new skills, learning or training
referralRoutes: Online enquiry via the Paddock Trust website
In person - via community venues and drop-ins
Partner referral, including Kirklees Council Employment & Skills Service

activities.name: One-to-one employment support
activities.summary: Starts with an assessment of the person's situation, skills and goals. Covers strengths and transferable skills, CVs, job applications and interviews, benefits and financial advice, and volunteering, training and education opportunities. Helps with barriers such as childcare, low confidence or lack of skills.
activities.duration: Flexible and open-ended, at the person's own pace

activities.name: Group workshops
activities.summary: Course-based workshops in community settings on personal development, wellbeing, goal setting, CV writing, job searching and interview techniques, alongside 1-to-1 guidance.
activities.duration: Course-based

activities.name: Connecting to local opportunities and services
activities.summary: Links people to local employers, vacancies, training providers and wider community support, including digital inclusion, information and advice, and wellbeing services delivered by Paddock Trust.
activities.duration: Ongoing

services.workExperience: Volunteering and work-related opportunities identified as part of the plan

services.name: Fitness for Work
services.whoFor: Kirklees adults aged 18 and over who are out of work, off sick or at risk of falling out of work through a health condition, and are ready to use physical activity to manage it.
locations: Huddersfield Leisure Centre
Batley Sports and Tennis Centre
Colne Valley Leisure Centre
Spen Valley Leisure Centre
eligibility: Aged 18 or over
Committed to making a long term lifestyle change
Clinically stable and compliant with their medication

AND one of: out of work due to ill health and unable to look for work as a result; had sickness from work due to ill health for more than 7 days in the last 6 months; at risk of falling out of work due to ill health
exclusions: Resting tachycardia over 100bpm
Systolic blood pressure over 180mmHg and/or diastolic over 100mmHg
New or uncontrolled arrhythmias
Unstable diabetes
Unstable angina
Unstable mental health status
Unstable or acute heart failure
Symptomatic hypotension
Febrile illness
Any other condition which may be exacerbated by exercise
referralRoutes: Internal rerouting of Fitness for Health referrals who meet the eligibility criteria
Workplace liaison, health days and direct engagement with key local employers

activities.name: Fitness for Work
activities.summary: A structured 12-week physical activity programme with one weekly exercise-specialist-led session (studio class, water-based class or gym session) plus full KAL membership for the duration. Aimed at people with mental health or musculoskeletal conditions. Individual support from a Specialist Exercise Co-ordinator and Exercise Referral Specialists.
activities.duration: 12 weeks

activities.name: Post 12 week programme
activities.summary: Access to KAL's active movers membership (full access), recommendations of suitable classes and groups, graduation events and gym floor support.
activities.duration: Ongoing

services.name: Flippin' Pain (incl. Why We Hurt)
services.whoFor: Anyone in Kirklees living with persistent pain lasting more than three months, and the professionals who support them.
locations: Digital/online - accessible to Kirklees residents from any location
eligibility: Kirklees resident living with persistent (chronic) musculoskeletal (MSK) pain of more than 3 months who can benefit from a digital patient activation programme
Professionals across the integrated care system (healthcare, local authority, physical activity and leisure) who want the competence and confidence to support people with chronic pain
referralRoutes: Via a referring professional - email invitation to the hosting platform
Link to the programme information web page, then opt in

selfReferral.note: Yes, where a link has been shared by a referring professional or through campaign activity

activities.name: Why We Hurt - digital patient activation programme
activities.summary: Seven short (about 5 minute) videos with transcripts, interactive exercises, a library of information and a peer discussion forum, helping people understand pain and manage it, including staying physically, socially and economically active. Endorsed by the British Pain Society and the European Pain Federation. Optional health coach moderation.
activities.duration: Unlimited access for up to 12 months from sign-up

activities.name: Targeted workforce development
activities.summary: Education on modern pain science for professionals working across the integrated care system.

services.notes: 1,000 Why We Hurt licences funded by NHS West Yorkshire ICB. DPIA completed; Cora Health is data controller.

services.name: Get Set Goal
services.whoFor: Employers and self-employed people in Kirklees - primarily SMEs and sole traders - whose staff are experiencing ill health and at risk of falling out of work.
locations: University of Huddersfield campus
Onsite at business premises and other event venues
Online
eligibility: Employees (including in SMEs, independent care sector, VCSE and healthcare organisations) and self-employed people experiencing ill health. Focus for 2026-27 is SMEs and sole traders, but larger employers are still supported
At risk of falling out of work due to ill health
Committed to making a long term lifestyle change
exclusions: Under 18

activities.name: One-to-one wellbeing coaching
activities.summary: Tailored light-touch wellbeing support using goal setting to improve lifestyle choices and manage conditions, with signposting to other Healthy Working Life services. Wellbeing coaching only - it is not a counselling service. Delivered by University of Huddersfield healthcare students under clinical supervision.
activities.duration: Up to 6 weekly sessions, Monday to Friday 9am-4pm excluding bank holidays

activities.name: Events in businesses or the community
activities.summary: Awareness raising, initial health checks and the chance to book one-to-one sessions.
activities.duration: One-off or regular

activities.name: Wellbeing workshops
activities.summary: Interactive workshops tailored to the business or organisation, for example managing stress, improving sleep and mental wellbeing.
activities.duration: Usually 20-30 minutes

activities.name: Health checks
activities.summary: Basic checks of blood pressure, oxygen level, pulse and respiration rate. Around 7% of people checked between April 2025 and March 2026 were signposted to their GP.
activities.duration: 5-8 minutes per person

services.name: Health & Wellbeing Hub
services.whoFor: Kirklees College students - mainly 16-19 year olds, plus adult and apprentice learners - needing wellbeing and employability support.
locations: Kirklees College campuses - five sites in Huddersfield and two in Dewsbury, with delivery across North and South Kirklees
eligibility: Is a Kirklees College student (including adult learners and apprentices)
At risk of falling out of education or training due to ill health, or health or wellbeing is affecting participation, progress or sustained employment
exclusions: Not a student at Kirklees College

activities.name: Health and Wellbeing Coaching
activities.summary: Early, holistic, work-focused support from the Student Service Hub: one-to-one coaching, on-campus health services (health checks, BACP-accredited counselling plus TAC Access online counselling, screenings), group activities and workshops, and supported inclusive work opportunities. Employment support through the on-site Job Shop with the DWP Jobs and Careers Service, including a Disability Employment Advisor.

activities.name: Embedding health and wellbeing across the college
activities.summary: Health programmes in the personal development curriculum, staff training including mental health first aid, student mental health ambassadors, and a school nurse pilot.

services.name: Individual Placement and Support for Change Grow Live service users
services.whoFor: Change Grow Live service users in Kirklees aged 18 and over who want to move into paid work.
locations: 20 Manchester Road, Huddersfield HD1 3HJ
3 Wellington Street, Dewsbury WF13 1LY
eligibility: Aged 18 or over and in treatment at Change Grow Live
Out of work, or in work but at risk of losing their job because of substance use and/or ill health
Consents to receive input from the IPS service and has a GP registered within Kirklees
exclusions: Only wants to look at voluntary work or education

activities.name: Individual Placement and Support
activities.summary: A 'place then train' approach matching people in recovery with paid work they want to do. An Employment Specialist builds a vocational profile, engages employers, supports CVs and interviews and agrees reasonable adjustments, then supports the person and their employer once in work.
activities.duration: Job coaching/placement up to 9 months; follow-along support for the first 4 months in work

services.name: Individual Placement and Support for Severe Mental Illness (SMI)
services.organisation: South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
services.whoFor: Adults in Kirklees with severe and complex mental health needs, under secondary care, who want to find or keep paid work.
locations: Folly Hall Mills, St Thomas Road, Huddersfield, HD1 3LT
Beckside Court, 286 Bradford Road, Batley, WF17 5PW
eligibility: Currently receiving support from secondary care mental health services (Core, Enhanced or Early Intervention in Psychosis teams)
Committed to remaining in or entering paid employment
In work and struggling, off sick, or in work and seeking a different role to improve wellbeing - or looking for work
exclusions: Mild to moderate mental health conditions
Solely physical health conditions
Only wants to look at voluntary work or education
Not currently under the care of secondary care mental health services
referralRoutes: Online self referral - electronic 'expression of interest' form under 'Referrals' on the service webpage

selfReferral.note: Yes, via the online expression of interest form

activities.name: Work retention support using the principles of IPS
activities.summary: Employment specialists work with community mental health services to explore interests, skills and goals, build an employment plan and address barriers. Rapid, intensive support from referral, support for both the person and their employer, help with disclosure and reasonable adjustments, and information about workplace rights.
activities.duration: Time-unlimited follow-along support for as long as the person wishes

services.name: Kirklees Employment Service
services.whoFor: Kirklees adults aged 18 and over with experience of mental ill health - including autism and other neurodivergent conditions, hidden disabilities, a learning disability where mental health support is the primary need, or dementia in a community setting - who want paid work. Also advises employers.
locations: Huddersfield base
Dewsbury base
Community venues across Kirklees
Remote - telephone, Teams and email
eligibility: Aged 18 or over and living in Kirklees
Currently or previously experiencing mental ill health, from low-level stress and anxiety to enduring severe problems - a medical diagnosis is not required; or has autism or a hidden disability
Has a goal of moving towards employment, education, training, volunteering or a placement, and is committed to working on agreed actions between sessions
Employers in Kirklees seeking advice on supporting employees' mental health are also eligible
exclusions: Under 18
Not ordinarily resident in Kirklees - people funded by a statutory body outside Kirklees are not eligible unless that agency spot purchases a place
referralRoutes: Practitioner referral - community psychiatric nurses, psychologists, consultant psychiatrists, occupational therapists, Job Centre Plus and other partner agencies

activities.name: One-to-one adviser support
activities.summary: Support from a named adviser, face to face, by phone, over Teams or email. An Employment Support Plan is agreed and reviewed at least every six months. Includes benefits guidance, careers information and supported job search, plus peer support workshops.
activities.duration: Contact within 3 working days of referral, initial meeting within 10 working days; typically a 6-month timeframe

activities.name: Job retention and job change support
activities.summary: Helps people experiencing mental ill health at work to stay in their job or move to a more suitable role, including agreeing adjustments and in-work support when starting a new job.
activities.duration: Tailored to need

activities.name: Peer support workshops and groups
activities.summary: For people not yet ready for one-to-one support, or who prefer groups: assertiveness, self-esteem, resilience, confidence to work and ways to wellbeing. Online and in person.
activities.duration: Rolling programme

activities.name: Volunteering and Peer Champion opportunities
activities.summary: Roles where people draw on their own experience to support others and build skills and confidence.

activities.name: Employer advice
activities.summary: Advice for employers on supporting employees with mental ill health: awareness and first aid training, reasonable adjustments, mental health champions, and specialist advice on employing people with autism, neurodivergent conditions, dementia or hidden disabilities.
activities.duration: On request

services.name: Kirklees Talking Therapies Employment Advice
services.organisation: South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (NHS Kirklees Talking Therapies)
services.whoFor: Kirklees Talking Therapies service users with common mental health conditions who want to find, keep or return to work.
locations: Across Kirklees, via Kirklees Talking Therapies venues and remote appointments
eligibility: Aged 17 or over, receiving or referred for Kirklees Talking Therapies treatment for a common mental health condition

Employment or career goals are part of their recovery - for example off work and anxious about returning, planning a phased return, at risk of losing work, looking for a first job, or wanting to change role
exclusions: Not a Kirklees Talking Therapies service user
Needs urgent mental health support - contact the Kirklees 24-hour Single Point of Access team on 01924 316830
referralRoutes: Online self referral via the Talking Therapies assessment route
Via in-house teams - the therapist may invite the person to an employment advisor appointment
Practitioner referral - health professionals via the information for professionals route

selfReferral.note: Yes - self-refer to Talking Therapies by phone or online, then access employment advice through the service

activities.name: Integrated employment advice alongside therapy
activities.summary: Employment advisors work jointly with therapists. One-to-one, client-led support on goals, CVs, gaps in employment, disclosure, applications and interviews, training needs, and an agreed action plan. Free and confidential. In person, by phone, video or the SilverCloud platform.
activities.duration: Usually around six appointments, extended where needed

activities.name: Job retention and workplace support
activities.summary: Helps people stay in work while managing mental health: reasonable adjustments, relationships at work, re-establishing contact with the workplace and phased returns.

services.name: My Way Forward
services.whoFor: Young people in Kirklees aged 16-25 who need help moving towards education, training or work.
locations: Brian Jackson House, Huddersfield
Community settings, e.g. Batley and Dewsbury Libraries
eligibility: Aged 16 to 25
Not in education, employment or training (NEET) with health concerns, including mental health
exclusions: Claiming Universal Credit with a requirement to actively look for work

activities.name: My Way Forward
activities.summary: 1:1 coaching on career opportunities, barriers and benefits; peer group sessions including social hubs and job clubs (online and in person); confidence and resilience activities; support to access health and wellbeing services; basic skills and job-specific training; volunteering and work experience; peer mentoring; and for some, job search, CV and interview help.
activities.duration: Open-ended, depending on need

services.name: Pathways to Possibilities (Proper Job Theatre Company)
services.whoFor: Economically inactive Kirklees residents aged 18+, particularly people with health conditions or disabilities, who want to build skills and confidence and take a next step into learning, volunteering or work.
locations: Proper Job Theatre Company Ltd, 46/47 Byram Arcade, Westgate, Huddersfield HD1 1ND
Community settings across Kirklees
Remote support (a mix of face-to-face and remote)
eligibility: Lives in Kirklees
Has the right to live and work in the UK
Economically inactive (of working age), particularly with health conditions or disabilities
exclusions: None specified - if the Trailblazer element is not suitable, the person will be supported via the most appropriate alternative option
referralRoutes: Email the delivery partner programme address (to be confirmed)

activities.name: Pathways to Possibilities
activities.summary: Three strands: health and wellbeing (confidence, resilience, social connections); engaging and building confidence for learning; and preparation for employment. Connects people to volunteering, learning and employment opportunities. 50 places available.
activities.duration: Programme starts 1 September 2026; referrals close 1 March 2027. No fixed duration - flexible and person-centred

services.workExperience: Yes - volunteering and work experience opportunities
services.notes: Webpage and self-referral route still to be confirmed in the source document.

services.name: Pathways to Possibilities (Fusion Housing)
services.whoFor: Economically inactive Kirklees residents aged 18+, particularly people with health conditions or disabilities, who want to build skills and confidence and take a next step into learning, volunteering or work.
locations: Fusion Housing Dewsbury Hub, Empire House, Wakefield Old Road, Dewsbury WF12 8DJ
Community settings across Kirklees
Remote support (a mix of face-to-face and remote)
eligibility: Lives in Kirklees
Has the right to live and work in the UK
Economically inactive (of working age), particularly with health conditions or disabilities
exclusions: None specified - if the Trailblazer element is not suitable, the person will be supported via the most appropriate alternative option
referralRoutes: Email the delivery partner programme address (to be confirmed)

activities.name: Pathways to Possibilities
activities.summary: Three strands: health and wellbeing (confidence, resilience, social connections); engaging and building confidence for learning; and preparation for employment. Connects people to volunteering, learning and employment opportunities. 50 places available.
activities.duration: Programme starts 1 September 2026; referrals close 1 March 2027. No fixed duration - flexible and person-centred

services.workExperience: Yes - volunteering and work experience opportunities
services.notes: Webpage and self-referral route still to be confirmed in the source document.

services.name: REAL Employment
services.whoFor: Kirklees adults aged 18 and over with learning disabilities, autism or additional needs seeking paid, sustainable employment.
locations: Civic Centre 3, High Street, Huddersfield, HD1 2TG
Dewsbury Town Hall, Wakefield Old Road, Dewsbury, WF12 8DG
eligibility: Lives in Kirklees and is aged 18 or over
Has a learning disability, is autistic, or has associated additional needs with a substantial adverse effect on day-to-day activities, lasting or expected to last 12 months or more
A formal medical diagnosis is not required
exclusions: Zero rejection policy - where REAL cannot meet a person's needs they signpost to appropriate services
Work experience placements are not offered as a standalone service
referralRoutes: Online self referral - simple form, around 5 minutes (a valid personal email address is needed): https://my.kirklees.gov.uk/service/Jobs___Contact_REAL_Employment
Referral by a family member, carer or professional using the same online form

activities.name: Supported employment and job matching
activities.summary: Job Coach support to match interests and skills to a job the person wants, including job searching, applications and interview techniques. Training can be part of the journey.

activities.name: Employer support
activities.summary: Works with employers who have vacancies to match candidates to the role and support the placement.

services.workExperience: No - not offered as a standalone service

services.name: Supporting Working Carers
services.organisation: Carers Count Kirklees (delivered by Cloverleaf Advocacy)
services.whoFor: Kirklees employers supporting staff who have unpaid caring responsibilities, and working carers themselves (supported through their employer).
locations: Online - 30-minute awareness sessions and one-to-one Teams calls
In person - employer forums (e.g. The Zone, Huddersfield) and employer drop-ins
On site at employer premises by arrangement
eligibility: Employers and organisations in Kirklees - managers, HR teams, mental health first aiders and anyone supporting staff wellbeing - who want to identify, engage, support and retain unpaid carers
Employees with unpaid caring responsibilities at risk of reducing hours or leaving work are supported indirectly through their employer
referralRoutes: Online booking for awareness sessions, training and forums (Eventbrite)

selfReferral.note: Yes - employers can register directly via any route

activities.name: Employer awareness training
activities.summary: A 30-minute online session on supporting employees who care, and to meet the team.
activities.duration: 30 minutes, repeating dates through the year

activities.name: One-to-one employer support
activities.summary: A one-to-one Teams call, then tailored support to identify carers in the workforce and put practical policies and culture in place.
activities.duration: Ongoing, tailored

activities.name: Employer forums
activities.summary: Quarterly forums for peer learning and awareness raising.
activities.duration: Quarterly, 1.5 to 2 hours

activities.name: Employer training session
activities.summary: Free online training on legal duties and carers' rights, recognising and supporting carers, reducing discrimination risk and managing flexible working.
activities.duration: 90 minutes, repeating dates through the year

services.notes: The source document lists named individuals' email addresses for this scheme; they are left out here until it is decided whether they should be public.

services.name: Wellness to Work
services.whoFor: Kirklees residents aged 18 and over with a health condition or disability affecting their ability to get or keep a job.
locations: Princess Royal Health Centre, Greenhead Rd, Huddersfield HD1 4EW
Batley Health Centre, 130 Upper Commercial St, Batley WF17 5ED
Dewsbury Health Centre, Wellington Road, Dewsbury WF13 1HN
eligibility: Aged 18 or over, living in Kirklees, with a health condition or disability affecting ability to get or keep a job
Out of work due to ill health, OR in work but at risk of falling out of work due to ill health (including musculoskeletal conditions and/or vocational rehabilitation needs)
Committed to remaining in or entering paid employment

activities.name: Wellness to Work
activities.summary: A personalised holistic assessment of barriers (health, confidence, skills, general wellbeing), clinical triage where needed, and a dedicated Employment Navigator and health professional who build an action plan. Includes MSK fast-track physiotherapy and occupational therapy vocational rehabilitation. Connects people to partners such as Get Set Goal, Kirklees Active Leisure, Kirklees College and Third Sector Leaders.
activities.duration: 3-6 months, with coordination for up to 3 months afterwards, plus in-work support for people who get a job

services.name: Healthy Working Life Community Grants Programme
services.status: Future - not yet open to referrals. Grants awarded; no information on individual grant-funded schemes until awards are confirmed
services.whoFor: Economically inactive Kirklees residents, reached through voluntary and community organisations funded by the programme. Grants go to VCSE and grassroots organisations, not individuals.
locations: Community settings across Kirklees - hyperlocal delivery by VCSE and grassroots organisations
eligibility: Economically inactive residents, particularly those with health conditions or disabilities, and other priority groups
exclusions: People who are in work or actively seeking work
referralRoutes: Delivery is by funded VCSE and grassroots organisations; participant access routes will be confirmed once grants are awarded

selfReferral.note: To be confirmed following grant awards

activities.name: Community grants to VCSE and grassroots organisations
activities.summary: Grants of 3,000 to 10,000 pounds for single organisations and up to 20,000 pounds for joint applications, funding community-based pre-employment and wellbeing activity. Organisations must be registered on the Kirklees Grant Access Point.
activities.duration: Projects start by 1 October 2026 at the latest

services.workExperience: Yes - where offered by funded projects
